canonical_statement: For every natural number n and every complex-valued function f on the real Euclidean space R^n which is square-integrable with respect to mathlib's volume measure, the normalized L2 Fourier transform of the L2 class represented by f has the same L2 norm as that class.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; Domain n abbreviates EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n); f : Domain n -> Complex; hf : MemLp f 2 volume; the target is Prop in Lean universe 0.
conclusion: The L2 norm of the Fourier transform of hf.toLp f equals the L2 norm of hf.toLp f.

degenerate_cases: The zero-dimensional Euclidean space is included. Infinite-dimensional spaces, real-valued codomains, non-L2 functions, unnormalized transforms, and arbitrary LCA groups are excluded.
